correctness.rationale: Deleting the new vertex from a spanning tree of the root-weighted augmentation designates exactly one root per forest component, so the matrix-tree cofactor is the multiaffine root enumerator. Substitution of signs computes the unnormalized Walsh sum with no positivity requirement. In the bipartite Schur complement the off-diagonal block has rank one and both diagonal blocks are invertible for m,n≥2, yielding the determinant prefactor and the product of the two reciprocal-diagonal sums. Its vanishing gives the exact zero-product equality; each weight pair contributes binomial multiplicity (eigenvalues for different pairs need not be distinct). The even-even equality is blocked modulo 2. At balanced odd d, write Q=d²−1 and c=(d−1)/2. Same-side weights cannot give equality except at (c,c); opposite displacements a and −b require Q(a−b)=2ab with 0<2ab≤Q/2, impossible. Stirling gives 2/(πd) for the resulting relative nullity. For d,d+1 the zero equation determines v=(d²−1)u/[d(d+2)−2u] where u=d−x and v=y. For 1≤u≤d, the positive difference u−v is strictly below one: the denominator is at least d², and u(2d+1−2u)≤(2d+1)²/8<d² for d≥2. Thus only u=v=0 remains, giving exactly one zero character. The computation supports, but does not prove, the all-size classifications.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An exact unsigned root histogram gives the signed polynomial by a binomial or Krawtchouk transform, so it subsumes raw enumeration. It does not tell which alternating sums vanish or why there are no other zero shell pairs for these infinite subfamilies.

value.rationale: The exact kernel measures lost Walsh modes in a natural forest-root convolution. Proving zero loss for both even shores, an explicit central-binomial defect for odd balanced shores, and one lost mode for consecutive shores exposes distinct behavior on natural infinite families, useful beyond raw root enumeration.
residual_risks: No simple classification of all remaining unbalanced pairs, condition-number theorem, or gap bound is claimed.
